Sentiment over time ------------------------------------------------------------
Dark themes reflected in sentiment of story overtime: 


```{r}
dorian_words <- dorian |>
  mutate(linenumber = row_number()) |>
  unnest_tokens(word, text) 


dorian_words |>
  inner_join(bing_sentiments) |>
  count(index = linenumber %/% 80, sentiment) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(sentiment = positive - negative) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = index, y = sentiment)) +
    geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_smooth(se= F)
```
Guide for annotations: https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/annotate.html



Side note: Direct comparison does not work with earnest. 

```{r}
earnest_words <- earnest |>
  mutate(linenumber = row_number()) |>
  unnest_tokens(word, text) 

earnest_words |>
  inner_join(bing_sentiments) |>
  count(index = linenumber %/% 20, sentiment) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(sentiment = positive - negative) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = index, y = sentiment)) +
    geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_smooth(se= F) +
  annotate("segment", x = 70, xend = 70, y = -10, yend = 10,
  colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 100, y = 7.5, label = "Algernon and Cecily meet")
```

Less clear arc, and sentiment analysis does not work as well with such a sarcastic and witty work. For example, patch of negative lines at index 75, when algeron and cecily are joking about being "wicked". Part of the joke is how un-wicked, but perfectly friendly, light hearted, and flirtatious the scene is. 






Vocabulary by character---------------------------------------------------------
```{r}
earnest_book <- str_flatten(earnest$text, " ")

lines <- str_split_1(earnest_book, "(?=(JACK\\.|ALGERNON\\.|CHASUBLE\\.|MERRIMAN\\.|LANE\\.|LADY BRACKNELL\\.|GWENDOLEN\\.| GWENDOLEN\\.|MISS PRISM\\.))" )

name_line <- as_tibble(lines) |>
  mutate(character = str_extract(value, "JACK\\.|ALGERNON\\.|CHASUBLE\\.|MERRIMAN\\.|LANE\\.|LADY BRACKNELL\\.|GWENDOLEN\\.| GWENDOLEN\\.|MISS PRISM\\."), 
         line = str_remove(value, "JACK\\.|ALGERNON\\.|CHASUBLE\\.|MERRIMAN\\.|LANE\\.|LADY BRACKNELL\\.|GWENDOLEN\\.| GWENDOLEN\\.|MISS PRISM\\.")) |>
  select(character, line) |>
  filter(!is.na(character))
```
